title_fr: La vie privée et la gestion de l'identité en ligne (DDN233)
description_fr:
Les employés qui travaillent en ligne éprouvent un nombre croissant de préoccupations liées à la protection de la vie privée et à la cybersécurité qui découlent auteur de leurs activités professionnelles que personnelles. Ce cours fournit un aperçu du paysage de la protection de la vie privée en ligne et propose des stratégies pour contrer les menaces et gérer son identité en ligne. Les participants apprendront à évaluer leur empreinte numérique et découvriront des pratiques exemplaires pour gérer et protéger leur identité en ligne.


Sujets traités :


·       apprendre à mieux connaître les préoccupations en matière de cybersécurité liées à la protection de la vie privée;

·       connaître les outils et les procédures visant à améliorer la protection des renseignements personnels numériques;

·       offrir des perspectives concernant la gestion de l’identité.


Remarques :


Ce cours est offert par le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité au coût de 750 $. Pour vous inscrire au cours et le payer, ou pour ouvrir une session ou créer un compte, visitez le Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité et faites une recherche en utilisant le titre du cours ou le code CYB103C.


Sur demande, ce cours peut être adapté à des groupes en fonction de leurs objectifs d'apprentissage professionnels ou encore de ceux de leur entreprise ou de leur ministère. Pour obtenir plus de renseignements sur ce service et sur ses coûts, écrivez au Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité, à education@cyber.gc.ca.

This online self-paced course explores different ways to monitor social media and highlights how social intelligence can improve organizational performance. Participants will learn best practices for gathering and analyzing social media data, and insightful ways to use social awareness strategies to deliver real business value.

Topics include:

- defining the business benefits of social intelligence
- setting up effective social media monitoring
- identifying the common sources of social media data
- analyzing social data effectively to uncover real business intelligence
- applying social intelligence findings strategically

title_en: Discover Cyber Security (DDN235)
description_en:
Digital technologies have quickly become an integral part of our daily lives, with new developments and security concerns emerging every day. This online self-paced course helps to build a greater awareness and understanding of the reality of cyber risks by exploring common security vulnerabilities and cyber threats, such as malware, password attacks and social engineering. Participants will learn to recognize potential threats and how to protect themselves, their digital information and the systems they use.

Topics include:

· defining cyber security and its importance

· protecting against malware and other cyber threats

· understanding Government of Canada security roles and policies

· adopting best practices

· pursuing additional security training opportunities

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for employees of the core public administration.

Learners will receive a certificate of completion after successfully completing the final quiz. Revalidation is required annually by completing Cyber Security Quest (DDN247) (recommended) or by redoing DDN235.

This course is offered in collaboration with the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

title_en: Introduction to Product Management in the Public Service (DDN236)
description_en:
An important goal of effective product management is to ensure that the product meets the needs of its intended users. This online self-paced course introduces the key concepts of product management and recommends best practices for creating products in a public service context. Participants will learn about product teams, including the different roles, responsibilities and skillsets of team members, as well as some of the tools available to assist them.

 

Topics include:

- introducing product management terminology
- guiding product development from conception to delivery
- defining the roles and responsibilities of product teams
- applying design thinking, Agile practices, and human-centred design approaches

 

Notes:

 

This course is intended for newcomers to product management in the public service, including project managers retraining as product managers, first-time product managers, product owners, and new employees working in product development teams.

The first step in the design process is to understand the problem space, which involves exploring the circumstances behind a problem. This online self-paced course presents the foundational methods and tools needed to identify and analyze problems that need solving. Participants will learn how to apply these discovery methods in their work and use sound problem framing to set up the next steps in the design process.

Topics include:

· identifying and framing the problem to be solved

· identifying the real people impacted by the problem

· exploring empathy mapping

· setting boundaries for solutions in a government context

· writing point-of-view problem statements

description_en:
Making the switch to digital technologies requires taking a close look at core business processes, organizational governance and customer experiences. This online self-paced course assembles a playbook of best practices for digital transformation that focus on the customer, mobilize operational processes and sustain the employee experience during a period of change. Participants will learn about the underlying business models and digital platforms that power digital transformation, along with the leadership capabilities required to make digital transformation a reality.

Topics include:

· focusing digital transformation on the customer experience

· recognizing the operational elements of digital transformation

· supporting business model transformation

· identifying the four major components of implementing digital transformation

description_en:
As the world and technology changes, organizations are constantly looking for new ways to adapt and transform themselves. This online self-paced course provides an overview of how to build digital dexterity within an organization to ensure its readiness for potential business opportunities. Participants will be introduced to the four characteristics of a digital organization and learn about strategies to sustain a successful digital transformation.

Topics include:

· setting strategies for building a digital-first mindset

· recognizing the common practices of digitally adept organizations

· identifying strategies for moving from a traditional to a digital organizational design

· identifying the four characteristics of digital dexterity: a digital-first mindset, digitized organizational practices, the human capabilities of an empowered digital workforce, and the resources to support it all

Topics include:

· identifying the requirements for innovation success

· taking leadership actions to overcome obstacles to innovation

· recognizing the characteristics of an innovation culture

· encouraging creativity and innovation in people

· identifying the steps and activities of a flexible innovation process

title_en: Ethical Considerations in Artificial Intelligence (DDN243)
description_en:
The use of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping how services are designed and delivered across the public and private sectors. This online self-paced course explores the foundations of artificial intelligence, its opportunities, potential risks, ethical considerations and the use of AI in the public sector. Participants will review the ethical implications of AI use in government, examine examples that highlight potential risks and challenges, and learn about methods to help address them.

 

Topics include:

 

·         exploring ethical principles for the responsible development and use of AI, including fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy and security

·         exploring common applications and best practices of AI use in the public service

·         recognizing key ethical challenges and identifying strategies to minimize risks

·         reviewing emerging AI standards, regulations and governance frameworks

The final step in the design process is to prototype and test the final iterations of a product or service. This online self-paced course presents the steps to take to create and test prototypes effectively. Participants will learn about the benefits of testing prototypes, evaluation methods and tools, and how to refine a prototype into a completed product or service.

Topics include:

· explaining  why prototyping is important

· designing hypothesis-driven prototypes

· using prototypes to test and validate hypotheses

· selecting the right tools to build prototypes of various fidelity levels

title_en: Cyber Security Best Practices (DDN250)
description_en:
Digital technologies have quickly become an integral part of our daily lives, with new developments and security concerns emerging every day. This course provides an overview of the various cyber security risks and threats that may be encountered in our professional and personal lives.  Participants will learn behaviours and strategies to mitigate these risks, such as choosing strong passwords, spotting and properly handling suspicious emails, and securing personal devices and social media accounts.

Topics include:

· identifying various cyber threats

· determining strategies, recommendations, steps, and behaviours to mitigate risks online

· implementing best practices that mitigate cyber risk and improve cyber hygiene

Notes:

This course is delivered by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security and has a cost of $750. To register and pay, or to sign in or create an account, visit the Cyber Centre Learning Hub and search for the course by title or by code CYB102C.

Upon request, this course can be tailored for groups to fit specific professional, business or departmental learning objectives. Email the Cyber Centre Learning Hub at education@cyber.gc.ca for specific details and costs.
title_fr: Pratiques exemplaires en matière de cybersécurité (DDN250)
description_fr:
Les technologies numériques sont rapidement devenues une partie intégrante de notre quotidien, s'accompagnant chaque jour de nouvelles avancées et préoccupations en matière de sécurité. Ce cours donne un aperçu des différents risques et menaces liés à la cybersécurité que l'on peut rencontrer dans notre vie professionnelle et personnelle. Les participants apprendront sur les comportements et les stratégies à adopter pour atténuer ces risques, comme choisir des mots de passe difficiles à deviner, repérer et traiter adéquatement les courriels suspects, et sécuriser les appareils personnels et les comptes de médias sociaux.

Sujet traités :

· reconnaître différentes cybermenaces;

· déterminer les stratégies et les comportement à adopter ainsi que les recommandations et les étapes à suivre pour atténuer les risques en ligne;

· mettre en place des pratiques exemplaires qui permettent d'atténuer les cyberrisques et d'améliorer la cyberhygiène.

Remarques :

Ce cours est offert par le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité au coût de 750 $. Pour vous inscrire au cours et le payer, ou pour ouvrir une session ou créer un compte, visitez le Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité et faites une recherche en utilisant le titre du cours ou le code CYB102C.

Sur demande, ce cours peut être adapté à des groupes en fonction de leurs objectifs d'apprentissage professionnels ou encore de ceux de leur entreprise ou de leur ministère. Pour obtenir plus de renseignements sur ce service et sur ses coûts, écrivez au Carrefour de l'apprentissage du Centre pour la cybersécurité, à education@cyber.gc.ca.

title_en: Transforming Government Services for the Digital Era (DDN251)
description_en:
To meet the high expectations surrounding the delivery of digital services, leaders throughout the Government of Canada must upskill to help guide this digital transformation. This online self-paced course, designed for executive leaders and other forward-thinking public servants, provides insight into how government services are currently being transformed or adapted to meet the digital demands of Canadians. Participants will learn about the need to adapt their leadership style and the new skills that are required for them to succeed in the digital era. 

Topics include: 

- exploring the evolution of government services 
- examining how governments are building and supporting digital platforms and organizations 
- explaining why getting government digital services right is so important 
- developing new leadership skills for the digital era 

Notes: 

Each week for eight weeks, participants will receive an email containing advice and guidance from David Eaves, Associate Professor in Digital Government at the University College London Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose.
Each email will include a short video (between 5 to 10 minutes) and a curated list of links to resources on public service transformation and digital leadership. At the end of the eight weeks, participants who viewed the videos will receive a certificate of completion.

description_en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping society, industries, and public services, making it essential for government leaders to understand its transformative potential and ethical implications. The AI Learning Accelerator Program for Executives examines the practical applications of AI, offering experiential training and insights into how AI can be used to address complex challenges and improve service delivery. Participants will be equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to lead AI initiatives that drive meaningful impact, while fostering innovation and collaboration across departments.

Le Programme d'accélération de l'apprentissage sur l'IA pour les cadres permet d'examiner les utilisations pratiques de l'IA et offre une expérience de formation concrète ainsi que des idées sur la manière dont l'IA peut servir à relever des défis complexes et à améliorer la prestation de services. Les participants acquerront les connaissances et les compétences nécessaires pour diriger des projets axés sur l'IA qui auront une incidence significative tout en favorisant l'innovation et la collaboration entre les ministères.

title_en: Applying Human-Centred Design (DDN253)
description_en:
Human-centred design (HCD) is a practice that places the needs, wants and experiences of people at the core of its approach. This course takes the form of an interactive seminar that explores how human-centred design can be achieved through innovative methods such as design thinking and behavioural science to improve government services. Participants will examine relatable case studies to learn how to engage with HCD principles, behaviours and impacts and how to integrate HCD best practices into their work practices.

 

Topics include:

 

·         understanding the HCD mindset and its principles

·         exploring real Government of Canada case studies that demonstrate HCD best practices

·         engaging in the discovery, definition, ideation, prototyping and testing phases

·         designing inclusive and accessible solutions

·         applying the HCD approach to Government of Canada products and services

 

Notes:

 

This course is facilitated by Dominira Saul, a design practitioner at Dffrnt, an Ottawa-based strategic research and design consultancy that helps clients solve complex problems through creative, human-centred approaches.

title_en: Leading Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Culture in the Workplace (DDN263)
description_en:
Adopting artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly and responsibly is presenting complex challenges for public sector leaders. This course serves as a virtual and interactive seminar for executives on what it takes to adopt new AI technologies and take the actions required to enable an AI culture change in the workplace. Through thoughtful discussion and by learning from experienced leaders in this field, participants will reflect on how AI-driven change impacts people and which leadership behaviours and change-management practices can best support them within Government of Canada realities and accountabilities.

 

Topics include:

·         assessing readiness for AI adoption

·         identifying leadership actions that enable culture change

·         supporting teams through uncertainty

·         strengthening capacity for responsible AI adoption

·         improving service and program delivery through AI

 

Notes:

 

This course is delivered as a virtual seminar and is available exclusively for employees at the EX level.

description_en:
Public servants who interact with data on a daily basis are expected to collect and use that data in a way that is ethical and unbiased. This online self-paced course focuses on the guiding principles of data ethics, including privacy, security, and the impacts of data-driven decisions on marginalized communities. Participants will learn how data ethics can help them navigate through some of the common ethical dilemmas associated with data while maintaining unbiased and neutral data practices.

- understanding what data ethics is and its importance
- identifying and mitigating potential biases
- exploring the guiding principles of data ethics
- building public trust in government data management

title_en: Using Generative AI in the Government of Canada (DDN321)
description_en:
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly transforming the content-creation process and offer many potential benefits to the Government of Canada. This course builds on the government’s Guide on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence by outlining key considerations when using these tools, including the importance of inclusive language and effective commands and prompts. Participants will gain the knowledge essential to navigating and applying this evolving technology through beginner-level demonstrations and applications led by specialists in the AI field.

 

Topics include:

 

·         exploring generative AI tools and identifying potential applications in the Government of Canada

·         understanding the principles of responsible use of generative AI

·         writing clear, specific and inclusive prompts to guide AI tools

·         evaluating the quality of AI-generated output

 

Notes:

 

To fully participate in this virtual, instructor-led course, participants will need their computers, as well as mobile devices with cameras capable of scanning QR codes.

 

The following resources are recommended reading for a deeper understanding of the course material:

·         Responsible use of artificial intelligence in the Government of Canada

- Guide on the use of generative artificial intelligence
title_fr: Utiliser l'IA générative au gouvernement du Canada (DDN321)
description_fr:
Les outils d’intelligence artificielle générative (IA) transforment rapidement le processus de création de contenu et pourraient présenter de nombreux avantages au gouvernement du Canada. Ce cours s’appuie sur le Guide sur l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle générative du gouvernement et souligne les principales considérations liées à l’utilisation de ces outils, dont l’importance de rédiger des requêtes efficaces et en langage inclusif. La participation au cours vise l’acquisition de connaissances essentielles pour comprendre et utiliser cette technologie en constante évolution, au moyen de démonstrations et d’applications de niveau débutant présentées par des spécialistes du domaine.

 

Sujets traités :

 

·         explorer les outils d’IA générative et déterminer ses applications possibles au gouvernement du Canada;

·         comprendre les principes d’une utilisation responsable de l’IA générative;

·         rédiger des requêtes claires, précises et en langage inclusif pour guider les outils d’IA;

·         évaluer la qualité des résultats de l’IA.

 

Remarques :

 

Pour participer pleinement à ce cours virtuel dirigé par un enseignant, il faut avoir à sa disposition son ordinateur et un appareil mobile doté d’une caméra pouvant balayer un code QR.

 

Les lectures suivantes sont recommandées pour bien comprendre le matériel du cours :

 

·         Utilisation responsable de l’intelligence artificielle au gouvernement

·         Guide sur l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle générative

title_en: Working with Disaggregated Data for Better Policy Outcomes (DDN323)
description_en:
Disaggregated data can help policy-makers develop more targeted and effective public policies by identifying the unique needs and challenges faced by different demographic groups. This online self-paced course explains data disaggregation, how it can inform the early stages of policy development, and how it can lead to better public policy outcomes. Through videos, interactive activities and case studies, participants will learn how to identify potential target groups and guide the formulation of government initiatives.

 

Topics include:

·         understanding what disaggregated data is and why it is important

·         reflecting on the impact of disaggregated data on policy outcomes

·         extracting and synthesizing key findings, and presenting them in data tables

·         framing messages that contain disaggregated data

 

Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

description_en:
The ability to analyze and use disaggregated data is essential for crafting policies that are both inclusive and effective. This online self-paced course takes a real-world issue—challenges faced by Black entrepreneurs in Canada—and chronicles the process that policy analysts can take to create actionable insights that will guide policy decisions. Participants will be prompted to think critically and solve problems related to disaggregated data.

•	using census data and charts to outline key findings about business ownership

•	analyzing disaggregated data to identify challenges faced by Black entrepreneurs in Canada

•	communicating findings from disaggregated data analysis


Notes:

This course was created in collaboration with Statistics Canada.

title_en: Policy Implementation Case Study: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development (FON102)
description_en:
The United Nation's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development is a global framework centred on an ambitious set of sustainable development goals, targets and indicators. This online self-paced course uses the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development as a case study to assist learners in gathering insights on the key considerations involved in the development of an effective and sustainable policy implementation strategy. Participants will share their ideas on how to identify a policy problem, select appropriate policy instruments, acknowledge the stakeholder environment, conduct a risk assessment, and evaluate implementation success.

Topics include:

• selecting policy instruments, such as financial measures, regulations, information and services
• implementing policy goals with observable results
• examining potential risks and mitigation strategies regarding the policy implementation process
• consulting and informing individuals impacted by policy implementation

Notes:

This course requires a time commitment of 2 hours each week for 6 weeks (12 hours total). Each week, participants will be asked to complete reading, writing or research assignments or participate in an online discussion forum.

- defining, measuring, monitoring, and evaluating results when adjusting policies, programs and services

title_en: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Introduction (FON202)
description_en:
When developing regulatory proposals, consideration of their economic, environmental and social impacts is a critical and often mandatory first step. This course provides a general introduction to cost-benefit analysis (CBA) and demonstrates how to apply CBA to federal regulatory initiatives. Participants will become familiar with the foundational steps to completing a CBA and learn how to develop solid baseline and regulatory scenarios.


Topics include:


- understanding the analytical steps in the CBA process
- identifying costs and benefits for different stakeholder groups
- applying best practices for collaborating and meeting reporting requirements
- reviewing the information found in a CBA report


Notes:


This course is divided into two 3-hour sessions, offered on the same day of the week, one week apart, over a period of two weeks.


This course is for federal public servants at all levels who work in the regulatory field. It may also benefit those who are new to the regulatory process or to cost-benefit analysis, or anyone who has a general interest in these areas. Learners who are already familiar with the basic concepts of cost-benefit analysis are encouraged to register for Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Application (FON203) instead.

title_en: Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Application (FON203)
description_en:
Cost-benefit analysis (CBA) is a structured approach used to identify and assess potential outcomes to better inform decisions. This course explores the intricacies of the CBA process and emphasizes how rigorous analysis is pivotal to supporting evidence-based decision-making, specifically by federal regulators. Participants will acquire the skills needed to conduct a basic CBA to support the creation of a regulatory impact analysis statement (RIAS).

Topics include:

•	revisiting the theoretical foundations of CBA •	building CBA models •	assessing potential positive and negative outcomes •	supporting quantitative, qualitative and monetizing analyses •	summarizing results and drafting recommendations for decision-makers

Notes:

To receive a certificate of completion, participants must attend two virtual instructor-led sessions over the course of two weeks. They must prepare for the instructor-led sessions by also completing five online self-paced modules:


1. Self-paced modules 1 and 2
2. Virtual instructor-led session 1 (week 1; 2.5 hours)
3. Self-paced modules 3, 4 and 5
4. Virtual instructor-led session 2 (week 2; 2.5 hours)

Learners who are unfamiliar with the basic concepts of cost-benefit analysis are highly encouraged to complete Cost-Benefit Analysis for Federal Regulators: Introduction (FON202) before registering for this course.
title_fr: Analyse coûts-avantages dans la réglementation fédérale : application (FON203)
description_fr:
L'analyse coûts-avantages est une approche structurée servant à déterminer et à évaluer d'éventuels résultats afin de prendre des décisions éclairées. Ce cours porte sur les particularités de l'analyse coûts-avantages et met l'accent sur le fait qu'une analyse rigoureuse est essentielle à la prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes, en particulier dans la réglementation fédérale. Les participants acquerront les compétences nécessaires pour faire une analyse coûts-avantages de base qui servira à l'élaboration d'un résumé de l'étude d'impact de la réglementation.

Sujets traités :

•	revoir les notions de base de l'analyse coûts-avantages; •	créer des modèles d'analyse coûts-avantages; •	évaluer les résultats éventuellement négatifs et positifs d'un règlement; •	réaliser des analyses quantitatives, qualitatives et monétaires; •	résumer des résultats et rédiger des recommandations à l'intention des décideurs.

Remarques :

Pour obtenir un certificat d’achèvement, les participants doivent assister à deux séances virtuelles dirigées par un enseignant sur une période de deux semaines. Ils doivent par ailleurs se préparer aux séances virtuelles en suivant les cinq modules à rythme libre, selon l’ordre suivant :


1. Modules 1 et 2 à rythme libre
2. Séance 1 en salle de classe virtuelle dirigée par un enseignant (semaine 1; 2,5 heures)
3. Modules 3, 4 et 5 à rythme libre
4. Séance 2 en salle de classe virtuelle dirigée par un enseignant (semaine 2; 2,5 heures)

Les personnes qui ne connaissent pas les notions de base de l'analyse coûts-avantages sont fortement encouragées à suivre le cours Analyse coûts-avantages dans la réglementation fédérale : introduction (FON202) avant de s'inscrire à ce cours-ci.

title_en: Values and Ethics Foundations for Employees (FON301)
description_en:
As part of their orientation to the public service, it is essential that all employees learn about the core values and expected behaviours shared by public servants across Canada. This online self-paced course introduces the foundational public sector values and ethical behaviours presented in the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector. Through informative exercises and scenarios, participants will learn how to identify values and ethics principles and how to integrate them into their work routines and practices.


Topics include:

·       understanding the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector

·       identifying and applying values and ethics principles

·       recognizing conflict of interest, ethical dilemmas and accountability issues

 

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for employees of the core public administration.
title_fr: Fondements des valeurs et de l'éthique pour les employés (FON301)
description_fr:
Dans le cadre de leur orientation à la fonction publique, les personnes employées doivent apprendre ce que sont les valeurs fondamentales du secteur public et les comportements attendus d'elles. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente les valeurs fondamentales et les comportements éthiques présentés dans le Code de valeurs et d'éthique du secteur public. Au moyen d'exercices et de mises en situation instructifs, les participants apprendront à reconnaître les valeurs et les principes éthiques, ainsi qu'à les intégrer à leur quotidien et à leurs pratiques de travail.


Sujets traités :

·       comprendre le Code de valeurs et d'éthique du secteur public;

·       cerner et appliquer les principes liés aux valeurs et à l'éthique;

·       reconnaître les conflits d'intérêts, les dilemmes éthiques et les responsabilités.

 

Notes :

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les employées de l’administration publique centrale.

title_en: Values and Ethics Foundations for Managers (FON302)
description_en:
Public service managers have an obligation to apply the core values of the public sector in their decisions, behaviours and work environments. This online self-paced course helps managers to better understand the foundational concept of values and ethics, and how to apply it when dealing with conflicts of interest, ethical dilemmas, harassment situations and other issues of workplace well-being. Through practical exercises and case studies, participants will identify, discuss and apply the key principles and policies related to values and ethics in the public sector.   


Topics include:

·       identifying values and ethics policies and legislation

·       reviewing policies concerning post-employment measures

·       applying values and ethics to work situations and practices

 

Notes:

This course has been determined by the Secretary of the Treasury Board to be mandatory for first-time managers.
title_fr: Fondements des valeurs et de l’éthique pour les gestionnaires (FON302)
description_fr:
Les gestionnaires de la fonction publique sont tenus d'appliquer les valeurs fondamentales du secteur public dans leurs décisions, leurs comportements ainsi que leur milieu de travail. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre permet aux gestionnaires de mieux comprendre les fondements des valeurs et de l'éthique et d'apprendre à s'en servir pour gérer des conflits d'intérêts, des dilemmes éthiques, des situations de harcèlement et des problèmes liés au mieux-être en milieu de travail. Les participants, au moyen d'exercices pratiques et d'études de cas, seront appelés à déterminer les principes et les politiques clés en matière de valeurs et d'éthique du secteur public, à en discuter et à les appliquer.  


Sujets traités :

 ·       connaître les politiques ainsi que les lois et les règlements en matière de valeurs et d'éthique;

·       examiner les politiques relatives aux mesures concernant l'après-mandat;

·       appliquer les valeurs et les principes d'éthique à des situations et à des pratiques de travail.

 

Notes:

Ce cours a été jugé obligatoire par le Secrétariat du Conseil du Trésor pour les nouveaux et nouvelles gestionnaires.

title_en: Who We Work For (FON304)
description_en:
Understanding how Canada's non-partisan federal public service serves the democratically elected government is fundamental to all public servants. This online self-paced course examines the functions of Parliament, the Government of Canada and the federal public service, as well as the organizational relationships between these entities. Participants will gain a foundational understanding of how government works and the vital part they play in its critical operations.

Topics include:   

·       recognizing the role and structure of the federal government and how Canada is governed

·       differentiating departments, central agencies and their respective functions

Les participants comprendront mieux le fonctionnement du gouvernement et le rôle central qu'ils jouent dans les grandes opérations de ce dernier.

Sujets traités :

title_en: Navigating Federal Decision-Making and Accountability (FON306)
description_en:
Understanding the mechanics of government decision-making is valuable knowledge for public servants who are engaged in the policy process and who support the parliamentary process. This course provides participants with an opportunity to better understand their role and their impact within the federal government structure. Participants will learn how their contributions help to achieve the goals of government, whether this be developing or evaluating policy, or implementing programs or services.

 

Topics include:

 

·       exploring the federal policy cycle

·       identifying the main actors in the federal decision-making process

·       outlining the roles and responsibilities of the federal government and its governance structure

·       examining the three phases of the federal decision-making process: policy cover, funding and authorities

·       identifying the mechanisms through which Parliament and the courts ensure accountability of the executive branch

 

Notes:

 

This is an intermediate-level course that provides an in-depth analysis in the government decision-making process. It is intended for executives, aspiring executives, policy analysts and program officers. The course will benefit learners who:

 

·       implement government programs and services

·       support the implementation of government programs and services

·       maintain and develop policy

·       monitor and evaluate the work of government

 

This course is divided into two three-hour sessions and relies on open group discussions during the virtual sessions where the facilitator will offer answers or clarifications during the discussions and encourage participants to reflect on how the course content applies to their different roles throughout the public service.

 

An understanding of how government works is needed to fully engage and participate in the course. Participants are encouraged to complete How the Canadian Government Works: Setting the Stage for Results (FON305) prior to taking this course.

title_en: HR-to-Pay for Employees (FON308)
description_en:
All employees have a role to play in being paid accurately and on time. This online self-paced course presents realistic scenarios that explain how employees in the federal public service are paid and common situations that can affect employee pay. Participants will learn about their responsibilities related to HR-to-pay processes and how submitting information on time is important for accurate and timely employee pay.


Topics include:


- understanding the foundational elements of HR-to-pay
- explaining common situations that can result in changes to employee pay
- identifying the different roles involved in ensuring accurate and timely employee pay
- using practical tools and job aids to complete HR-to-pay actions
- outlining the HR-to-pay responsibilities and entitlements in accordance with federal acts, policies, directives, and collective agreements


Notes:

The core public administration is defined in the Financial Administration Act as “the departments named in Schedule I and other portions of the federal public administration named in Schedule IV.” The Treasury Board serves as the employer for these organizations.

•  understanding the mechanisms of governance, oversight and accountability

•  maintaining communications with the public and the language of work

•  ensuring equitable participation and positive measures related to Part VII of the Act

title_en: Introduction to Gender-based Analysis Plus (INC101)
description_en:
Gender-based Analysis Plus (GBA Plus) is both an analytical tool and a process that supports decision-making and the development of responsive and inclusive policies, programs and initiatives. This online self-paced course provides an introduction to GBA Plus and explains how it goes beyond sex and gender to consider other identity factors that interact to shape social, health, and economic opportunities and outcomes. Participants will learn how to turn their GBA Plus insights into action by reflecting on recurring barriers to accessing government services and exploring ways to mitigate them.


Topics include:


- defining the key concepts of GBA Plus
- applying foundational GBA Plus concepts and processes
- identifying how GBA Plus can enhance an initiative
- meeting the diverse needs of those most impacted
- anticipating and mitigating barriers to accessing or benefitting from GBA Plus


Note:

The “Plus” in Gender-based Analysis Plus acknowledges that this approach goes beyond sex and gender differences to include other identity factors, like race, ethnicity, religion, age, language, education, and mental or physical disability.

title_en: Positive Space Initiative: 2SLGBTQIA+ Awareness (INC111)
description_en:
Diversity and inclusion are essential for building a modern, high-performing public service. This course introduces the concepts, terminology and vocabulary related to gender and sexual diversity, as well as the importance of Positive Space and how to become an ally. Participants will discuss issues relevant to the 2SLGBTQIA+ communities and learn to contribute to a safer, more inclusive public service.
 
Topics include:
 
·      reviewing terminology and vocabulary
·      exploring 2SLGBTQIA+ history in Canada
·      defining Positive Space and why it is important
·      understanding heteronormativity, cis-normativity and privilege
·      being an ally
 
Notes:
 
Learners who wish to become a Positive Space Ambassador will need to complete Positive Space Initiative: 2SLGBTQIA+ Awareness (INC111) and Positive Space Initiative: Becoming an Ambassador for 2SLGBTQIA+ Inclusion (INC112), or equivalents.
 
2SLGBTQIA+ = Two-Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, aromantic, agender and people who identify as being part of sexual and gender diverse communities.

title_en: Positive Space Initiative: Becoming an Ambassador for 2SLGBTQIA+ Inclusion (INC112)
description_en:
While much progress has been made, the 2SLGBTQIA+ communities still face challenges with heterosexism, genderism, transphobia and homophobia, which can lead to individuals feeling unsafe at work. This course explains what it means to be a Positive Space ambassador and prepares individuals to offer support to their colleagues as a Positive Space ambassador in the workplace. Through scenarios and practical exercises, participants will learn behaviours that can help bring diversity and inclusion into the modern workplace.


Topics include:

- defining the role of a Positive Space ambassador
- outlining helpful behaviours of ambassadors
- reviewing different support methods

  \

2SLGBTQIA+ = Two-Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, aromantic, agender and people who identify as being part of sexual and gender diverse communities.
title_fr: Initiative Espace positif : Devenir personne ambassadrice de l'inclusion des personnes 2ELGBTQIA+ (INC112)
description_fr:
Même si de nombreux progrès ont été réalisés, les communautés 2ELGBTQIA+ sont toujours confrontées à des problèmes d'hétérosexisme, de binarisme de genre, de transphobie et d'homophobie, qui peuvent conduire les personnes à se sentir en danger au travail. Ce cours explique en quoi consiste le rôle des personnes ambassadrices de l'Espace positif et prépare ces personnes à offrir du soutien à leurs collègues dans le milieu de travail. Par des mises en situation et des exercices pratiques, les personnes participantes découvriront les comportements qui peuvent contribuer à intégrer la diversité et l'inclusion dans le milieu de travail moderne.

 

Sujets traités :

- définir le rôle d’une personne ambassadrice de l'Espace positif;
- présenter les comportements bénéfiques des personnes ambassadrice;
- examiner diverses méthodes de soutien.

 

Remarques :

 

Pour exercer efficacement le rôle de personne ambassadrice de l'Espace positif, il faut avoir suivi de la formation pour se sensibiliser à l'Espace positif avant de s'inscrire à ce cours‑ci, comme le cours Initiative Espace positif : Sensibilisation aux réalités 2ELGBTQIA+ (INC111) ou l'équivalent.

 

2ELGBTQIA+ = personnes aux deux esprits, lesbiennes, gaies, bisexuelles, transgenres, queers, intersexuées, asexuelles, aromantiques, agenres et celles qui indiquent leur appartenance à divers groupes sexuels et de genre.

title_en: Addressing Disability Inclusion and Barriers to Accessibility (INC115)
description_en:
Being accessible and inclusive means allowing unimpeded access or full participation without exclusion or exception. This online self-paced course challenges common assumptions and beliefs about people with disabilities and aims to shift the perspective from the impairment to the barrier. Participants will learn about the different barriers faced by people with disabilities and how to make their workplaces and the services they provide inclusive, accessible and barrier free.

Topics include:

· acknowledging the personal impact of exclusion

· learning from the experience of people with disabilities

· identifying the often-simple steps needed to make a document or service accessible

· finding tools and resources to support your work and to share with others

Notes:

Every day, people with disabilities face barriers related to employment, communications, information technology, procurement, transportation, and the built environment (buildings and public spaces). Other barriers are attitudinal in nature: sometimes invisible, unintentional or systemic and most often perpetuated by stigma or misunderstanding. Learn more about the Government of Canada's commitment to Making an accessible Canada for persons with disabilities.

This course initiates a timely and meaningful conversation on how to identify and address the impacts of systemic racism in the workplace. Participants will advance their understanding of the challenges that accompany discrimination and learn concrete actions for confronting racism and creating meaningful change within the federal public service. 

Topics include:   

· distinguishing between racism and systemic racism 

· contextualizing systemic racism 

· acknowledging systemic racism in the workplace 

· supporting a respectful and inclusive workplace 

· addressing systemic racism in the federal public service 

 Notes:   

This participation-based course is intended for learners who are ready to advance their knowledge of race, racism, identity and inequality in a context where systemic racism is understood to be a human rights issue. Participants must have a solid understanding of the historical context of racism and how it has contributed to current societal inequities.   

This advanced course requires participants to work in small groups on topics related to identifying and addressing racial issues, such as micro-inequities, micro-aggressions, racial profiling, gaslighting, etc. Participants must have knowledge of these concepts before attending this course. 

 Prerequisites:   

Prior to registering for this course, participants must have completed [Advancing
the Conversation on Systemic Racism: Self-Assessment (INC116)](https://catalogue.csps-efpc.gc.ca/product?catalog=INC116&cm_locale=en) as a prerequisite.

title_en: Fostering an Inclusive Workplace (INC118)
description_en:
Understanding concepts such as equity, diversity and inclusion is essential for building a more respectful and inclusive workplace for all employees. This online self-paced course introduces what it means to be equitable, diverse and inclusive, and how to support greater inclusion in the federal workplace. Participants will reflect on their own biases and privileges, while exploring practical actions they can take to foster inclusion and other areas to further their learning.   

Topics include:   

· reflecting on unconscious biases, privilege, intersectionality and equity 

· being an ally for 2SLGBTQIA+ communities 

· building an accessible public service 

· promoting anti-racism 

· exploring the importance of mental health and well-being   

Notes: 

 This introductory course serves as a starting point for anyone who wants to learn about equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) to help create, foster and promote an inclusive workplace for everyone.   

The course is organized into five modules, which participants can complete over 5 consecutive or non-consecutive days, depending on their availability. Upon full completion of each module, they will receive an email inviting them to proceed to the next day's module. Each module should take approximately 15 to 45 minutes to complete. Participants must successfully complete all five course modules to receive a certificate of completion.   

Schedule:   

· Day 1, Module 1: Introduction to Inclusion 

· Day 2, Module 2: 2SLGBTQIA+ Inclusion 

· Day 3, Module 3: Accessibility 

· Day 4, Module 4: Anti-Racism 

· Day 5, Module 5: Mental Health
title_fr: Favoriser un milieu de travail inclusif (INC118)
description_fr:
Il est essentiel de comprendre des notions comme l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion pour créer un milieu de travail plus respectueux et inclusif pour tous les employés. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre explique ce que sont l'équité, la diversité et l'inclusion, et comment améliorer l'inclusion en milieu de travail à la fonction publique fédérale. Les participants réfléchiront à leurs biais et à leurs privilèges, tout en découvrant des mesures pratiques qu'ils pourront prendre pour favoriser l'inclusion et en approfondissant leur apprentissage en lien avec d'autres domaines. 

 Sujets traités :   

· réfléchir aux biais inconscients, aux privilèges, à l'intersectionnalité et à l'équité; 

· être une personne alliée des communautés 2ELGBTQIA+; 

· bâtir une fonction publique accessible; 

· promouvoir la lutte contre le racisme; 

· explorer l'importance de la santé mentale et du bien-être. 

 Remarques :   

Ce cours d'introduction sert de point de départ pour toute personne qui souhaite approfondir ses connaissances au sujet de l'équité, de la diversité et de l'inclusion en vue de créer et de favoriser un milieu de travail inclusif pour tous.   

Le cours se compose de cinq modules, que les participants peuvent terminer dans une période de cinq jours consécutifs ou non consécutifs, selon leur disponibilité. Après avoir terminé un module, ils recevront un courriel les invitant à passer au module du jour suivant. Chacun des modules prend environ
15 à 45 minutes à terminer. Les participants doivent terminer les cinq modules pour obtenir un certificat d'achèvement.   

Calendrier :   

· Jour 1, module 1 : Introduction à l'inclusion 

· Jour 2, module 2 : Inclusion des personnes 2ELGBTQIA+ 

· Jour 3, module 3 : Accessibilité 

· Jour 4, module 4 : Lutte contre le racisme 

· Jour 5, module 5 : Santé mentale

title_en: Call It Out: Racism, Racial Discrimination and Human Rights (INC119)
description_en:
First steps towards understanding racism include being honest about our past, aware of intergenerational trauma, and informed about the impacts of racial discrimination in our society. Adapted from the Ontario Human Rights Commission, this online self-paced course explains the meaning of race, racism, and racial discrimination, and presents a historical overview of racism and racial discrimination in Canada. Participants will learn about the human rights protections under the Canadian Human Rights Act and will take away practical approaches for preventing and addressing instances of racial discrimination in their workplace.

Topics include:

· revisiting the history and root causes of racism
in Canada

· recognizing the historical and current-day implications
of racism in Canada

· identifying indications of race-based discrimination
and harassment in the workplace

· describing the different impacts that racism and
racial discrimination can have in people's lives

· identifying ways to address racism and racial discrimination
at work

title_en: Disability Management and Workplace Wellness (INC120)
description_en:
Disability management is a deliberate and coordinated effort to reduce the occurrence and effect of illness and injury on workforce productivity.
This online self-paced course outlines the disability management process for responding to work-related and non-work-related impairments and functional restrictions, including injuries, illnesses, disabilities and other limitations. Participants will learn about the legislative instruments and disability management tools that support workplace wellness for federal government employees, as well as the accommodation measures to consider when creating a remain-at-work or a return-to-work plan.   

Topics include:    

- defining "disability" and "disability  management" 
- understanding workplace health and wellness 
- facilitating a return to the workplace after an  extended absence 
- reviewing the key components of a successful disability  management program 
- understanding the employer's obligations under  workplace accommodation 

 Notes:   

Learn more about Disability management in the federal public service.

title_en: Becoming an Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Ally and Agent for Change (INC121)
description_en:
Working in a diverse and inclusive organization offers many personal and professional benefits, including improved health and wellness, greater engagement at work, and increased innovation and creativity. This online self-paced course presents strategies for becoming an advocate for equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in the workplace. Participants will learn about the key concepts of allyship and how to communicate more inclusively, while gaining awareness of their own values and social perspectives.   

Topics include:   

· defining the key concepts of allyship 

· building awareness of one's values and social perspectives 

· creating connections through inclusive communication 

· identifying specific actions for becoming an EDI change agent 

· demonstrating inclusion using the RISE steps (Respect, Include, Support, and Engage)

title_en: Adopting an Inclusive Mindset at Work (INC122)
description_en:
Ensuring inclusion in the workplace requires the active participation and support of all employees, no matter their role. This online self-paced course articulates the power of inclusion and identifies best practices for encouraging greater equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in an organization. Participants will learn how to apply inclusive recruitment and hiring principles, as well as how to commit to making inclusion part of their employee onboarding process.

Topics include:

· adopting an inclusive mindset

· leveraging the power of inclusion

· supporting EDI at work

· recruiting and hiring based on the principles of inclusion

· committing to EDI throughout your career

description_en:
Understanding our implicit biases is an essential step in developing an inclusive mindset. This online self-paced course describes some of the most common unconscious biases and how to recognize them in the workplace. Participants will be encouraged to reflect on their own biases and the importance of being inclusive when making decisions.

Topics include:

· defining the key characteristics of implicit/unconscious biases

· recognizing common biases at work

· moving beyond bias and towards inclusion

· exploring techniques for identifying your own biases

title_en: Responding to Unconscious Bias (INC133)
description_en:
A critical step in building strong diverse teams is to recognize, understand and overcome hidden prejudices. This course examines the consequences of unconscious biases and presents practical strategies to mitigate them in the workplace. By actively taking part in group discussions, participants will strengthen their ability to recognize and respond to their own biases, and will learn about concrete actions they can take to help foster a respectful and inclusive public service.  

Topics include:

•	recognizing unconscious biases

•	identifying where unconscious biases come from, and who has them

•	exploring strategies and tools to mitigate and respond to unconscious biases in the workplace

Notes:

This intermediate-level course is participation-based. It requires participants to work in small groups on topics related to identifying and addressing unconscious biases.  

Having a foundational knowledge of unconscious bias prior to attending the course is required. For this reason, participants must complete Moving from Bias to Inclusion (INC123) as a prerequisite.
title_fr: Agir contre les biais inconscients (INC133)
description_fr:
Pour créer des équipes solides et diversifiées, il est essentiel de reconnaître, de comprendre et de surmonter les préjugés cachés. Ce cours permet d'examiner les conséquences des biais inconscients et propose des stratégies pratiques pour les atténuer en milieu de travail. En prenant part de manière active à des discussions de groupe, les participants renforceront leur capacité à reconnaître leurs propres biais et à agir contre ceux-ci et découvriront des mesures concrètes pour contribuer à l'établissement d'une fonction publique respectueuse et inclusive.

Sujets traités :

· reconnaître les biais inconscients;

· déterminer d'où viennent les biais inconscients et qui en a;

· découvrir des stratégies et des outils pour atténuer les biais inconscients en milieu de travail et agir contre ceux-ci.

Remarques:

Ce cours de niveau intermédiaire est axé sur la participation. Les apprenants devront prendre part à des activités en petits groupes qui les aideront à reconnaître et à examiner les biais inconscients.

Il faut posséder des connaissances de base sur les préjugés et les biais inconscients pour assister à ce cours. Le cours Passer des biais à l'inclusion (INC123) est donc un préalable au cours.

title_en: Addressing Antisemitism in the Workplace (INC135)
description_en:
Canada's Anti-Racism Strategy 2024–2028 and Canada's Action Plan on Combatting Hate promote an inclusive and equitable society free of racism, where everyone can fully take part, thrive and feel safe. This online self-paced course defines antisemitism and introduces the social, psychological, and cultural factors that perpetuate it. Through a review of case studies and historical context, participants will develop skills to recognize antisemitism, challenge stereotypes, and demonstrate allyship to prevent and address harassment and discrimination in the workplace.


Topics include:

- exploring the roots and history of antisemitism
- understanding contemporary antisemitism in Canada
- examining antisemitism and stereotypes in the workplace
- identifying ways to support colleagues through allyship
- recognizing the impact of antisemitism on federal public servants


Related links:

- Canada's Action Plan on Combatting Hate

title_fr: Agir contre l’antisémitisme en milieu de travail (INC135)
description_fr:
La Stratégie canadienne de lutte contre le racisme 2024-2028 et le Plan d’action canadien de lutte contre la haine font la promotion d’une société inclusive, équitable et exempte de racisme, à laquelle chaque personne peut participer pleinement et où elle peut s’épanouir et se sentir en sécurité. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre présente une définition de l’antisémitisme ainsi que les facteurs sociaux, psychologiques et culturels qui le perpétuent. L’examen d’études de cas et de l’histoire de l’antisémitisme permettra l'acquisition de compétences pour détecter l'antisémitisme, remettre en question les stéréotypes et s'allier en vue de prévenir et de combattre le harcèlement et la discrimination en milieu de travail.


Sujets traités :

- explorer les racines et l’histoire de l’antisémitisme;
- comprendre l’antisémitisme contemporain au Canada;
- examiner les manifestations de l’antisémitisme et les stéréotypes en milieu de travail;
- trouver des moyens de soutenir ses collègues en devant une personne alliée;
- prendre conscience des répercussions de l’antisémitisme sur les fonctionnaires du gouvernement fédéral.


Liens connexes :

- Stratégie canadienne de lutte contre le racisme
- Plan d’action canadien de lutte contre la haine

title_en: Introduction to Intersectionality (INC137)
description_en:
The Government of Canada serves a wide range of diverse communities, and the decisions it makes can have far-reaching impacts on people from many different backgrounds. This course introduces public servants to the concept of intersectionality and demonstrates how they can apply it to better understand and support the varied experiences of the populations they serve. Participants will explore how overlapping social identities, such as race, gender, class, sexuality, and disability, shape lived experiences and contribute to systemic barriers, and learn how intersectionality can inform more inclusive policies, programs, and services.

Topics include:

- examining the history and foundations of intersectionality
- recognizing how different identities intersect and intertwine to shape lived experiences
- understanding how similar situations can affect people differently based on their identities
- applying an intersectional lens to the development of policies, programs, and initiatives

description_en:
Awareness of cultural bias is an important step towards building a respectful workplace and better serving the Canadian public. With a focus on understanding Indigenous Peoples, this online self-paced course demystifies the idea of unconscious cultural bias and explores issues of prejudice and discrimination. Through a series of self-reflection exercises, participants will discover the cultural competencies they need to build respectful relationships with First Nations, Métis and Inuit.

·       exploring cultures, worldviews, race and ethnicity
·       strengthening awareness of cultural differences
·       understanding personal biases, prejudices and discrimination
·       building culturally safe relationships with Indigenous Peoples

description_en:
Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples involves looking back at our history from an Indigenous perspective. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the historical relationship between Indigenous Peoples and the Government of Canada, from first contact to the present-day focus on rebuilding this foundational relationship. Participants will benefit from a broader understanding of the impacts of government decisions on Indigenous Peoples and Indigenous communities.
 
Topics include:
 
·       identifying the key legislation within the Canadian political framework
·       assessing the impacts of Indian Residential Schools, the Sixties Scoop and the child welfare system
·       understanding the sacred connection to land in treaties and agreements
·       recognizing the rights of Indigenous Peoples
·       building a new relationship

title_en: Inuit in Canada (IRA105)
description_en:
Inuit awareness begins by understanding the unique life challenges that have shaped the Indigenous People of the Canadian Arctic, and which continue to impact their communities today. This online self-paced course provides a brief introduction to Inuit in Canada, including their traditions, governance structures and history. Participants will have an opportunity to reflect on a wide range of subjects, including the relationship between Inuit and the Government of Canada and the four distinct land claims agreements within the regions of Inuit Nunangat.
 
Topics include:
 
·      recognizing the diversity of Inuit across the country
·      understanding contemporary realities for Inuit in Canada
·      using respectful terminology
·      contemplating the historical and modern relationships between Inuit and the Government of Canada

Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples is important for all public servants. This application contains a wealth of general information about First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples, including key historical events and examples of reconciliation initiatives. title_en: Taking Steps Towards Indigenous Reconciliation (IRA107)
description_en:
Public servants play an important role in advancing reconciliation by helping to build stronger relationships at the working level between First Nations, Inuit, and Métis Peoples and the Government of Canada, and by fostering an inclusive workplace for Indigenous public servants. This online self-paced course supports the government's commitment to the value and outcomes of reconciliation by exploring in depth the four themes featured throughout the Indigenous Learning Series: recognition, respect, relationships, and reconciliation. By learning more about Indigenous realities, participants will be better equipped to support their departmental obligations towards reconciliation in a respectful, inclusive, meaningful and culturally sensitive manner.
Topics include:
- Recognition: acknowledging Indigenous experiences, expressions and narratives—past and present
- Respect: respecting Indigenous worldviews, knowledge systems, relationships with the land, cultural heritage, and Treaty rights
- Relationships: recognizing that Indigenous Peoples have a say in decisions that affect their rights and interests
- Reconciliation: working with Indigenous Peoples towards a better future
Notes:
Each Monday for four consecutive weeks, participants will receive an email assignment on an Indigenous-related topic, including recommended learning, resources and questions for personal reflection. Links will also be provided to supporting articles, podcasts, job aids, videos, and other resources.
At the end of the four-week course, participants who have successfully completed the assigned activities will receive a certificate of completion.
Schedule:
- Week 1: Recognition
- Week 2: Respect
- Week 3: Relationships
- Week 4: Reconciliation
title_fr: Prendre des mesures à l'égard de la réconciliation autochtone (IRA107)
description_fr:
Les fonctionnaires jouent un rôle important à l'égard de l'avancement de la réconciliation en aidant à établir des relations plus solides sur le plan du travail entre les Premières Nations, les Inuits et les Métis et le gouvernement du Canada ainsi qu'en favorisant un milieu de travail inclusif pour les fonctionnaires autochtones. Ce cours en ligne à rythme libre appuie l'engagement du gouvernement envers la valeur et les résultats de la réconciliation en explorant en profondeur les quatre thèmes mis en vedette tout au long de la Série d'apprentissage sur les questions autochtones : la reconnaissance, le respect, les relations et la réconciliation. En apprenant à mieux connaître les réalités autochtones, les participants seront mieux outillés pour appuyer leurs obligations ministérielles à l'égard de la réconciliation d'une façon respectueuse, inclusive, significative et qui tient compte des différences culturelles.
Sujets traités :
- Reconnaissance : reconnaître les expériences, les expressions et les récits des Autochtones, d'hier et d'aujourd'hui
- Respect : respecter les visions du monde, les systèmes de connaissances, les relations avec la terre, le patrimoine culturel et les droits issus de traités des Autochtones
- Relations : reconnaître que les Autochtones ont leur mot à dire dans les décisions qui ont une incidence sur leurs droits et leurs champs d'intérêt
- Réconciliation : collaborer avec les Autochtones pour un avenir meilleur
Remarques :
Chaque lundi pendant quatre semaines consécutives, les participants recevront un devoir par courriel sur un sujet lié à une question autochtone, y compris l'apprentissage recommandé, les ressources et les questions aux fins de réflexion personnelle. Des liens seront également fournis vers des articles de référence, des balados, des outils de travail, des vidéos et d'autres ressources.
À la fin du cours de quatre semaines, les participants qui auront réussi les activités demandées recevront un certificat d'achèvement.
Horaire :
- Semaine 1 : Reconnaissance
- Semaine 2 : Respect
- Semaine 3 : Relations
- Semaine 4 : Réconciliation

title_en: Revitalizing Voices: Navigating the Indigenous Languages Act (IRA110)
description_en:
Indigenous languages are integral to the cultural identity and heritage of Indigenous Peoples in Canada, yet many are at risk of disappearing. This online self-paced course provides an overview of the Indigenous Languages Act, highlighting its objectives and the broader context of Indigenous languages revitalization efforts. Participants will gain insights into the significance of Indigenous languages, and the role of public servants in supporting their preservation and revitalization.

Topics include:

·       understanding the purpose and provisions of the Indigenous Languages Act

·       exploring foundational documents related to Indigenous language rights

·       examining current efforts and strategies for Indigenous language revitalization

·       recognizing the importance of Indigenous languages to cultural identity

·       identifying the implications of the Act for public service roles and responsibilities

Notes:

This course replaces the job aid Revitalizing Indigenous Voices Through the Indigenous Languages Act (IRA1-J13).

title_en: Reconciliation Begins With Me (IRA141)
description_en:
Fostering an understanding of reconciliation and the importance of renewed relationships with Indigenous Peoples is a government priority. This course is designed to address the professional development and training requirements of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Call to Action #57. Following respectful protocols, participants will discover little-known historical facts, learn about the impacts of Residential Schools and the rights of Indigenous Peoples, and better understand the obligations of public servants towards Indigenous Peoples.

Topics include:

- understanding the history and diversity of First Nations, Métis and Inuit cultures and communities
- exploring the cultural competencies required for working with Indigenous Peoples and communities
- recognizing the impacts of government policies and practices

Notes:

This course is currently being offered virtually and has been converted into five learning modules: (1) Truth and Reconciliation, (2) Historical Timeline, (3) Talking About the Truth, (4) Roles and Responsibilities of Public Service Employees, and (5) What is Your Call to Action. Participants are asked to prepare for the weekly moderated conversations (three in total) by watching a video, reading a report, or working in a group exercise.

For offerings which start after March 31, 2021, these five modules will be delivered within one week (Three sessions of 2.5 hours).

The workshop presents 5 learning modules: Truth and Reconciliation, Historical Timeline, Talking about the truth, Role and Responsibility of public service employees and What is your Call to Action.

Pre-work for each session is required. This may consist of watching a video, reading an article or reflecting on an issue to discuss as a group.
title_fr: La réconciliation commence par moi (IRA141)
description_fr:
La compréhension de la réconciliation et l'importance du renouement des relations avec les peuples autochtones sont des priorités du gouvernement. Ce cours est conçu pour répondre aux exigences en matière de formation et de perfectionnement professionnel concernant l'appel à l'action no 57 de la Commission de vérité et réconciliation. En suivant des protocoles respectueux, les participants découvriront des faits historiques peu connus, se renseigneront sur les conséquences des pensionnats et les droits des peuples autochtones et comprendront mieux les obligations des fonctionnaires envers les peuples autochtones.

Sujets traités :

- comprendre l'histoire et la diversité des communautés et des cultures des Premières Nations, des Métis et des Inuits;
- explorer les compétences culturelles nécessaires pour travailler avec les peuples et les communautés autochtones;
- reconnaître les répercussions des politiques et des pratiques du gouvernement. 

Remarques :
Ce cours est offert virtuellement en ce moment et a été converti en cinq modules d'apprentissage : 1) Vérité et réconciliation, 2) Trame historique, 3) Parlons de la vérité, 4) Rôle et responsabilités des fonctionnaires et 5) Appel à l'action. Les participants doivent se préparer aux conversations hebdomadaires avec modérateur (trois au total) en regardant une vidéo, en lisant un rapport ou en faisant un exercice de groupe.

Pour les offres qui commencent après le 31 mars 2021, ces cinq modules seront livrés en une semaine (trois séances de 2,5 heures).

L'atelier présente 5 modules d'apprentissage : Vérité et réconciliation, Trame historique, Parlons de la vérité, Rôle et responsabilités des fonctionnaires et puis, votre Appel à l’action.

Un travail préparatoire pour chaque session est nécessaire. Les travaux préparatoires peuvent être composés du visionnement d'une vidéo, de la lecture d'un article ou de la réflexion sur une question pour en discuter en groupe.

title_en: Cultural Competency: Indigenous Perspectives (IRA142)
description_en:
uilding cultural competency helps to strengthen inclusive workplaces and foster respectful relationships with Indigenous Peoples. This course explores the diversity of Indigenous cultures and perspectives by encouraging reflection on personal values, biases and worldviews. Participants will gain foundational knowledge about the impacts of intergenerational trauma, develop an understanding of Indigenous knowledge systems, and build skills to contribute to culturally safe and respectful work environments.

Topics include:

exploring Indigenous worldviews and two-eyed seeing

understanding prejudice, bias, and discrimination

examining privilege and its connection to bias and inclusion

recognizing intergenerational trauma and its impacts

understanding allyship and its role in creating culturally safe workplaces

Notes:

Participants are expected to complete short pre-session assignments, such as watching videos, reading articles, or reflecting on certain topics in advance, to discuss as a group. Some topics in this course may evoke strong emotions. Participants are encouraged to take breaks as needed or to seek support if required.

Participants are strongly encouraged to actively engage throughout this course, which includes numerous interactive activities designed to review and practise key content topics. Active engagement will help to reinforce learning and ensure that participants gain practical experience in applying the concepts.

The following courses are prerequisites:

- Reflecting on Cultural Bias: Indigenous Perspectives (IRA101)
- A Brief History of the Relationship Between Indigenous Peoples and the Government of Canada (IRA102)
title_fr: Compétence culturelle: perspectives autochtones (IRA142)
description_fr:
Acquérir des compétences culturelles contribue à renforcer l’inclusion sur le lieu de travail et à favoriser des relations respectueuses avec les Autochtones. Ce cours explore la diversité des cultures et des perspectives autochtones en encourageant la réflexion sur les valeurs personnelles, les préjugés et les visions du monde. Les participants acquerront des connaissances fondamentales sur les répercussions des traumatismes intergénérationnels, se familiariseront avec les systèmes de connaissances autochtones et obtiendront des compétences qui leur permettront de contribuer à la création d’environnements de travail respectueux et inclusifs culturellement.

Sujets traités :

- explorer les visions du monde des Autochtones et l’approche à double perspective;
- réfléchir aux biais, aux préjugés et à la discrimination;
- examiner les privilèges et leur lien avec les préjugés et l’inclusion
- comprendre les traumatismes intergénérationnels et leurs répercussions;
- comprendre le concept d’alliance et son rôle dans la création de lieux de travail inclusifs culturellement.

Remarques :

Avant le cours, les participants doivent effectuer de courtes activités préparatoires, comme visionner des vidéos, lire des articles et réfléchir à certains sujets dont ils discuteront en groupe.

Certains des sujets abordés dans le cours pourraient entraîner de fortes émotions. N’hésitez pas à faire des pauses et à demander de l’aide, au besoin.

Les cours suivants sont des prérequis :

title_en: An Introduction to Canada's Colonial History (IRA143)
description_en:
Learning about and understanding our shared history is an important step towards reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples. This course explores colonialism and other historical themes and events in a way that provides an opportunity to see Canada's history from a new perspective. Participants will learn how the relationships with First Peoples in Canada have developed over the past 500 years and how to begin the work of addressing the impact of this history on all Canadians.

Topics include:

- examining historical periods in the relationship between Indigenous Peoples and settlers
- reviewing themes and events in colonial history
- acknowledging the impacts of historical events on the lives of First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples today

Indigenous Peoples may face real barriers at each stage of the public service employment process. This course provides human resources specialists and managers with concrete ways to help facilitate the hiring, retention and advancement of Indigenous employees within the public service. Participants will gain an understanding of the realities that some Indigenous employees face in the public service, and will learn practices that can make a difference in supporting their careers.

Topics include:

- hiring and retaining Indigenous employees

- fostering the career development and talent management of Indigenous employees

title_en: An Introduction to Modern Treaties and Self-Government (IRA146)
description_en:
Modern treaties are nation-to-nation agreements between Indigenous Peoples, the federal government and provincial or territorial governments. This online self-paced course provides an introduction to understanding and respecting the unique role of modern treaties and self-government arrangements when working with Indigenous partners. Participants will learn how federal officials can support the implementation of modern treaties and self-government arrangements as a pathway towards reconciliation.


Topics include:


·   exploring the foundational concepts of modern treaties and self-government

·   discovering the history of modern treaty-making with Indigenous partners in Canada

·   understanding the role of public servants in the implementation of modern treaties and self-government

·   identifying the resources available for engaging with Indigenous partners

description_en:
Public service leaders are responsible for knowing their country's history and acknowledging how past decisions are still impacting Indigenous populations. This course for executives provides an overview of the key events that make up Crown-Indigenous relationships and that have historically had a negative impact on Indigenous populations. Participants will review the recommendations of several important reports that propose concrete ways to make amends and overcome mistakes from the past.

Topics include :

· acknowledging the harm created by the Indian Act

· recognizing Canada's colonial policies and practices, and their impacts

· raising awareness about reports that aim to improve the well-being of Indigenous Peoples

· taking concrete measures to advance reconciliation

· finding inspiration to actively work at renewing relationships with Indigenous populations

Notes :

This course is reserved for public service executives. Non-executives are invited to register for the non-executive equivalent An Introduction to Canada's Colonial History (IRA143) instead.

This course is a prerequisite for Building Meaningful Relationships with Indigenous Peoples (IRA172).

This course consists of two separate sessions of three hours each, delivered over two days.

This cohort-based program challenges executives to reflect on their personal leadership style and better equip themselves to lead organizational innovation while managing their ongoing accountabilities. title_fr: Programme de développement en leadership pour les cadres supérieurs (PDLCS) de niveaux EX-01 à EX-03 (LPL101)

Ce programme par cohorte incite les cadres à réfléchir à leur style de leadership personnel et à se doter des outils nécessaires pour diriger l'innovation organisationnelle tout en assumant leurs responsabilités courantes. Les participants, sous la direction de cadres supérieurs reconnus, seront exposés à des expériences et à des problèmes réels et auront l'occasion d'agir en vue de résoudre un problème précis avec leurs pairs.
